stories.primary_headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay releases water from Mettur Dam

primary_source.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay releases water from Mettur Dam
primary_source.content: Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Tuesday threw open the sluices of the Stanley Reservoir in Mettur, releasing water for irrigation in the fertile Cauvery Delta region after the dam’s water level touched 90 feet. The dam was not opened on its designated date of June 12 due to the non-availability of water, as Karnataka failed to adhere to the monthly schedule of water release stipulated by the Supreme Court.Dressed in a silk shirt and silk veshti, Vijay worshipped the water before showering it with flowers as a mark of releasing water from the dam, which is the lifeline of lakhs of farmers in the Cauvery Delta region comprising Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, and Mayiladuthurai districts.Tuesday was chosen for the dam’s opening since the water level reached 90 feet last week — following the established practice that water is released only when the level touches 90 feet to ensure sustained supplies over months. The water level at the dam stood at 91.56 feet, storage at 54.452 tmcft, and the inflow at 10,857 cusecs.Explainer | The Mettur dam and why water released from the reservoir is the lifeline for lakhs of farmers in Cauvery Delta regionThe discharge was increased to 5,000 cusecs at 4:00 PM from 3,000 cusecs at 11:00 AM, and further increased to 7,000 cusecs at 8:00 PM on Tuesday.“Water is being released through the dam powerhouse and tunnel powerhouse. The barrages have been informed to maintain the discharge without any deviation,” a senior government official told&nbsp;DH.Vijay drove from the Salem Airport to&nbsp;Mettur — a&nbsp;distance of 51 kilometers — with people lining both sides of the road to give him a rousing reception. After the event, Vijay visited a farmer's home, met residents near Mettur, interacted with them, gifted a saree to the farmer's wife, and posed for pictures with elderly women.While water from the dam is generally released for the cultivation of&nbsp;kuruvai&nbsp;(short-term crop) on June 12, the schedule could not be maintained this year.&nbsp;Kuruvai&nbsp;has effectively failed in the Delta region, with farmers claiming that paddy was cultivated on only about 2 lakh acres, down from last year’s record cultivation of 6.30 lakh acres.Samba&nbsp;is generally cultivated across an area of about 10.5 lakh to 11 lakh acres in the four districts.The water released from the Mettur Dam will be used for the&nbsp;samba&nbsp;(long-term crop) this year, with farmer associations urging cultivators to adopt direct-sowing methods to save time. The government plans to release about 1 tmcft of water a day for 45 days, relying on the onset of the Northeast Monsoon (NEM) in mid-October to sustain the crop.“Since we need water for the whole season, we are asking our people to sow the seeds directly instead of using the regular cultivation method. We need to conserve water and use the available water judiciously,” P.R. Pandian, general secretary of the Tamil Nadu Cauvery Farmers’ Association, told&nbsp;DH.

stories.primary_headline: Kyiv launches criminal probe into arms depot attack that killed dozens

primary_source.headline: Kyiv launches criminal probe into arms depot attack that killed dozens - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has announced a criminal investigation after a Russian attack on a warehouse storing munitions killed at least 37 people near Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv. “A criminal investigation is under way. All the facts must be established,” Zelenskyy said in a video shared on X Saturday. Zelenskyy denounced the “terrible negligence” on the part of those who stored explosives right next to residential buildings, and said that the Prosecutor General, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Security Service of Ukraine, and the Commander-in-Chief have “everything necessary for the investigation”. The Russian drone attack killed at least 37 people overnight on Friday in the town of Myla, near Kyiv’s western suburbs. Huge explosions followed the attack on the warehouse, which stored munitions, authorities said on Saturday. “Unfortunately, the number of dead in the Bucha district has risen to 37… Rescuers and all relevant services are continuing their operations at the scene of the tragedy,” the governor of the Kyiv region, Tymur Tkachenko, said on Telegram on Saturday. Tkachenko said that at least 50 residential buildings had been damaged in the attack, which caused a large-scale fire that spread to homes and a restaurant. Nearly 400 people ⁠⁠were being evacuated from the strike area, and dozens of injuries were reported. Among the dead was Taras Didych, mayor of the village of Dmytrivka, Tkachenko added.

stories.primary_headline: Ukrainian nuclear power plant without external power for over a week

primary_source.headline: Ukrainian nuclear power plant without external power for over a week - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power station in southeastern Ukraine has been without off-site power for more than a week, the world’s nuclear energy watchdog has warned. The plant, which Russia has occupied since 2022, is currently relying on emergency diesel generators, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said on Saturday. “The availability of diesel fuel is of paramount importance whenever a nuclear power plant loses off-site power,” IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant has not had a delivery from an off-site storage facility in about six months but was supplied with diesel on Thursday and Friday from another off-site location, the IAEA said. The Vienna-based agency is now trying to negotiate a local ceasefire to allow repairs to electrical lines. Zaporizhzhia is Europe’s largest nuclear power plant. It has not generated electricity since September 2022, over six months after Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February that year, but the plant’s reactors must be kept cool to prevent a meltdown of the fuel inside.

stories.primary_headline: Flood chased me as I ran for 20 minutes, Nepal tunnel engineer tells BBC

primary_source.headline: Flood chased me as I ran for 20 minutes, Nepal tunnel engineer tells BBC
primary_source.content: Pemba Dundu Tamang tells the BBC how he discovered some of his colleagues were missing after he escaped a flooded tunnel It started with a sudden, strong gust of air, says Pemba Dundu Tamang, whose team of about 30 was constructing the tunnel's concrete lining. The blast of wind sent plywood flying through the air and dislodged heavy machinery. Just outside, houses had already been swept away. "I ran towards the tunnel entrance," he said. "The water was chasing behind me and I was running ahead of it." Tamang lost several family members who were at home at the time. Nepal's death toll has exceeded 1,000 after last week's devastating floods, and officials say about 4,000 are missing. A number of the missing - potentially in the hundreds - are labourers like Tamang, working in a vast network of tunnels at hydropower sites along the river. Engineers have been pumping air into these tunnels as part of a huge rescue operation.

stories.primary_headline: Sexual assaults happening almost every day in Ceuta, prosecutors say

primary_source.headline: Sexual assaults happening almost every day in Ceuta, prosecutors say
primary_source.content: Some 5,000 migrants who entered Ceuta from Morocco are estimated to still be in the Spanish exclave That number meant there was almost one case every day, Ceuta's chief prosecutor Silvia Rojas said. She told El País newspaper migrant girls were "particularly vulnerable because of their irregular status in the territory". At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July and although most have returned, as many as 5,000 remain - leading to unrest in the autonomous city in North Africa and a crisis for Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Between 1,400 and 1,600 of the estimated 5,000 migrants still in Ceuta are children, according to Rojas. Among the suspected attackers are four Moroccans, three Spaniards and a Belgian, Efe news agency reports.

primary_source.headline: Manasi Parekh, who escaped Nepal-Tibet floods by hours, landed on oxygen after a ‘stupid’ mistake
primary_source.content: Actor Manasi Parekh’s experience of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) during the Kailash Yatra has sparked questions about whether washing hair at high altitude can trigger the condition. Experts clarify that AMS is primarily caused by reduced oxygen availability and rapid ascent, not by washing one’s hair. However, staying wet and cold at high altitudes can increase physical discomfort, fatigue and sleep problems, making acclimatisation more difficult. Travellers should ascend gradually, stay warm and dry, remain hydrated, eat adequately, rest and avoid alcohol and strenuous exercise during early acclimatisation. Symptoms such as worsening headache or nausea, difficulty walking, confusion, extreme drowsiness, breathlessness at rest or a persistent cough require urgent medical attention and descent to a lower altitude. People with heart, lung or other serious medical conditions should also consult a doctor before undertaking high-altitude trips or pilgrimages.

stories.primary_headline: Two dead and about 15 people missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon

primary_source.headline: Two dead and about 15 people missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: At least two people have been confirmed to have been killed and about 15 people remain missing after a major flash flood hit the Grand Canyon in the US state of Arizona, authorities said. The National Park Service (NPS) reported on Monday that a second body has been recovered as the search continued. The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered on Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the park service said earlier, without providing additional details. The flooding in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the Colorado River, wiped out footbridges over the creek and significantly altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and creating what appeared to be a new river rapid. Popular tourist spots, including the Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch and parts of the North Kaibab Trail, remained closed on Sunday while park officials surveyed the damage, the park said. Rafting trips on the Colorado River also have been halted for now. Parth Desai was hiking through a narrow passage in Bright Angel Canyon with a group of fellow doctors and a park ranger when the downpour started. “We saw the creek flood, waterfalls coming up out of nowhere; boulders, mud, landslides happening everywhere,” he told The Associated Press news agency.

stories.primary_headline: Pogacar to have surgery on broken collarbone after horrific Vuelta crash

primary_source.headline: Pogacar to have surgery on broken collarbone after horrific Vuelta crash - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar was sent hurtling head-over-handlebars in a frightening crash that forced him to pull out of the Spanish Vuelta. The Slovenian suffered a concussion and broke two bones, one of which will require surgery, after he appeared to lose control when a stone rolled across the road on Saturday. “Tadej has been diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions,” said UAE Team Emirates medical director Adrian Rotunno. “Fortunately, no other major injuries and no neurological fallout. He will require clavicle surgery, which will be delayed due to concussion precautions. Tadej remains under the care of our medical team and we’ll provide further updates following the surgery,” Rotunno added. Pogacar held a big lead in the Vuelta and was heavily favoured to win the title to complete a hat-trick of cycling’s three Grand Tours. But he crashed about 33km from the finish of the eighth stage. He tried to get back on his bike but could not carry on and walked to an ambulance. Race organisers confirmed he pulled out of the race. TV video showed Pogacar with cuts on his head, left arm and shoulder. He swerved to his right into other cyclists as he appeared to try to avoid something in the road. The Tour de France champion lost control and flew over his handlebars, hitting his head and shoulder.

stories.primary_headline: Haitian gangs release 13 captives after mass kidnapping in Kenscoff

primary_source.headline: Haitian gangs release 13 captives after mass kidnapping in Kenscoff - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The United Nations has announced that six children and seven women kidnapped last week in the hillside community of Kenscoff, Haiti, have been released. In a statement late on Friday, representatives from the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) used the news to call attention to the ongoing crisis unfolding in Haiti — and the toll it has taken on the country’s youth. “This release offers a rare moment of hope amid the violence threatening children in Haiti,” said Yannig Dussart, the group’s deputy representative in Haiti. “The Kenscoff abduction was not an isolated incident but another stark reminder of the scale and frequency of attacks on children across the country.” The freed captives were part of one of the largest mass abductions in recent memory in Haiti. On the night of August 23, an estimated 150 armed gang members are believed to have attacked Kenscoff, which sits on the hillsides overlooking the capital Port-au-Prince and the suburb of Petionville.

From fermenting plums in honey and pickling courgettes in vinegar brine to a British take on kimchi, there are many ways to make the most of the warm-weather harvestWhat’s the best way to preserve late-summer fruit and veg?Jess, by email
 Fruit, fruit everywhere, so try fermenting it in honey, says Rachel de Thample, author of The Fermentation Year (published in September). “I’m currently looking at a jar of blackberries, but whole plums would be gorgeous, too,” she says, especially when eaten with blue cheese – “or any cheese, really” – meat or fish; you can also use the syrup like maple syrup or cordial. De Thample packs the fruit into sterilised jars and pours in just enough honey to cover it: “If the fruit has a low acidity, add a spoonful of lemon juice or a splash of cider vinegar as well.” Pop on the lid and leave for a few weeks. “It gets fizzy, but it doesn’t get to that explosive stage, because it has quite a concentrated sugar content. It’ll keep for up to a year at room temperature, but I normally pop it in the fridge after a few weeks.”Kimchi is another option to keep Jess enjoying summer fruits all year round. “In Korea, apples and pears are traditional, but there’s a kimchi for every season and region,” says De Thample, who takes a British approach with a courgette, blackcurrant and strawberry number: “You can use up tomatoes in the paste, too.” Otherwise, if you have plums and damsons, take inspiration from Japanese umeboshi: “That has a high percentage of salt – I use 15% per 100g fruit. Layer the salt and plums in jars and, if it’s really dry, pour over water; otherwise, just crush a couple of the plums so their juices create a brine with the salt.” The brine can then be used like a plummy soy sauce, De Thample says: “Having a few jars stored away always makes me feel like I’m winning.” Damsons are also a dream in flavoured liquors, says Kenji Morimoto, regular Guardian contributor and author of Ferment: “That’s a really nice way to capture their flavour, and all you need is vodka, the fruit and rock [or granulated] sugar.Got a culinary dilemma? Email feast@theguardian.com Continue reading...

primary_source.content: He was Queen’s flamboyant frontman. She was his shy girlfriend, dreaming of marriage until they both realised he preferred men. Thirty-five years after his death, in the week he would have turned 80, Mary Austin talks about their unbreakable bondThere were four silver trunks in Mary Austin’s attic that she packed in the mid-1980s and hadn’t opened since. It was too painful. Almost 40 years on, in 2022, she opened one. It was crammed with lyrics from songs written by Freddie Mercury – Don’t Stop Me Now, Killer Queen, We Are the Champions and, of course, Bohemian Rhapsody. She shut the case. It was still too painful.“To say I was overwhelmed is an understatement,” she says. “I couldn’t look at the lyrics. I felt as I did when I originally packed them – that they were his personal belongings and I was being offered an opportunity to delve into them, and I couldn’t do that.” Eventually she asked her two sons to sift through the treasures on her behalf. stories.primary_headline: ‘I’m not nervous, I’m ready’: Tschabalala Self on racist vandals and her bold striding woman for the Fourth Plinth

primary_source.headline: ‘I’m not nervous, I’m ready’: Tschabalala Self on racist vandals and her bold striding woman for the Fourth Plinth
primary_source.content: The last time she displayed a sculpture in public in Britain, someone covered it in white paint. But, undeterred, the acclaimed artist is a placing a black woman in Trafalgar SquareTschabalala Self is relentlessly positive and unstoppably optimistic. The US artist is waiting for the unveiling of Lady in Blue, her new sculpture for the fourth plinth in Trafalgar Square, London, a towering, colourful painted bronze of a black woman striding (positively, optimistically) into the future. Self seems resolutely hopeful about the work, which is pretty impressive considering what happened to her last public sculpture in the UK. “Yeah,” she says, speaking from her home in upstate New York. “I mean, that was a completely racist act.”In 2022, Self unveiled Seated at Coal Drops Yard in King’s Cross, London. Like Lady in Blue, it was a vast, brightly painted bronze depiction of a black woman, this time seated demurely on a chair. After being shown at Coal Drops Yard without incident, it was moved to the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill-on-Sea, where the reception wasn’t quite as warm. “Within the first week,” says Self, “it was spraypainted white, but only on the skin of the sculpture.” As vandalism goes, it doesn’t get much more pointed, or racist. “The first feeling I had was just pain that my sculpture had been harmed. That someone had enacted violence on an object I had imbued with love and affection.” Continue reading...

sources.headline: How a South African town cleaned up its polluted river using stones, wood and sand

stories.brief: Scientists say system to treat contaminated wastewater offers a model for ensuring food security in a fast-warming climate. All it took to turn the murky, heavily polluted waters of South Africa’s Stiebeuel River into a resource clean enough for irrigating a community’s vegetable plots was a collection of stones, heat-treated wood and sand. Without chemicals and using renewable energy, researchers from the University of Cape Town are cleaning 36,000 litres of water, polluted by sewage, chemicals, and traces of drugs and medication, every day to make it usable for growing food in a fast-expanding informal settlement along the course of the river.

primary_source.headline: I climbed the career ladder and got my dream job at 30 - then I hit burnout
primary_source.content: Jo Hooper said she felt like someone had flipped a switch in her brain "I loved being good at it," said Jo, a former communications professional. But just after she landed her dream role at 30, Jo struggled with burnout and had to take time off work. Jo, now 39 and based in Penarth in the Vale of Glamorgan, said: "I wanted to be a head of communications by the time I was 30, which I did by doing all things you'd expect, working long hours, saying yes to everything including mad things like taking my boss's kids to school." I'm on a mission to convince people to work less "I genuinely thought these were all good opportunities, and I was going to grab them with both hands," said Jo.

stories.primary_headline: The 100 Best Easy Dinner Ideas for Right Now

primary_source.headline: The 100 Best Easy Dinner Ideas for Right Now
primary_source.content: The Weeknight 100 is back, with so many fast,  delicious dinner ideas for busy times. Emily Weinstein is the editor in chief of New York Times Cooking and Food, and the writer of the Five Weeknight Dishes newsletter. Why publish it in September and not January? It’s back-to-school season, of course, the turning of the dial. It’s that transition from the languid late days of summer, when routine has long ago dissolved into the pool’s chlorine, to the first bell and a newly crammed calendar. I’m a summer person, and yet I appreciate the energy and optimism of September. It’s a moment to reset, to block out a new schedule and lay in new habits, to buy clothes, swear that we’ll get to the gym, get a full night of precious sleep or map out a week’s worth of dinners and stick to them. I can’t help you with the gym. But I can help you with dinner. I’ve selected the 100 dinner recipes below for you to try. The emphasis is on efficient yet excellent cooking, recipes that are truly delicious and don’t take too much of your time. Everything on this list takes under an hour to make, and a vast majority are much faster than that.

primary_source.headline: Noughties garage track named TikTok's UK song of the summer
primary_source.content: Kyla's 2008 track has featured in nearly 650,000 videos posted in the UK over the summer The song gained popularity when it was first released in 2008, but it became known worldwide in 2016 when Canadian rapper Drake sampled it on his chart-topping single One Dance. It has now found a new audience by trending on TikTok, generating more than 500 million views from about 650,000 videos posted in the UK over the summer, according to the platform. Kyla, who created the song with her husband DJ Paleface, tells BBC Newsbeat it is "surreal" but "incredible" that Do You Mind is getting another moment nearly 20 years on. Kyla joined singer Jorja Smith on stage at All Points East festival last month to perform the track together "Back in 2016, even though it had all that success, it still felt like: 'Oh, it's because you're with Drake'," she says.

stories.primary_headline: Analogue dairy crackdown: What it means for your food and health

primary_source.headline: Analogue dairy crackdown: What it means for your food and health
primary_source.content: Following increased scrutiny of analogue dairy products, experts say the key concern is not that all dairy alternatives are unsafe, but whether consumers clearly know what they are eating. Analogue dairy products may differ from traditional dairy in ingredients and nutritional value, with some containing less protein or calcium and higher levels of saturated fat or sodium. Vegans and those avoiding animal-based dairy can still benefit from clearly labelled plant-based alternatives, but people with lactose intolerance or milk-protein allergies should carefully check ingredient and allergen labels. Experts advise consumers to look beyond names such as cheese, paneer or cream, especially when ordering food, and focus on transparency, ingredients and overall nutritional quality.

stories.primary_headline: Houseplant hacks: can a lint roller banish pests?

primary_source.headline: Houseplant hacks: can a lint roller banish pests?
primary_source.content:
It’s a great detection tool, but if your plant is infested with thrips or spider mites it may not be enough …The problem
 The worst pests are the ones you can’t see; thrips and spider mites are tiny and very good at hiding on the undersides of leaves, in leaf joints and along stems. By the time you notice the damage – silvery streaks, speckling or fine webbing – the infestation is usually well under way. Early detection is the difference between a quick fix and a full-blown outbreak.The hack
 Use a sticky lint roller to pick up pests that are hard to see. The idea is it works as both a detection tool, and a light physical intervention, lifting adults and eggs before they multiply. Continue reading...

Of 24 novels written across 30 years, only the first four – A Start in Life, Providence, Look at Me and Hotel du Lac – are about a single woman pining for love. stories.primary_headline: Mrunal Thakur’s fitness coach Rohit Nair on her workout routine, diet, and mindset

primary_source.headline: Mrunal Thakur’s fitness coach Rohit Nair on her workout routine, diet, and mindset
primary_source.content: Actor Mrunal Thakur’s fitness routine focuses on building strength, improving movement, stamina and overall athleticism rather than chasing quick transformations or a number on the scale. Her coach Rohit Nair combines strength training, Pilates, functional exercises, mobility work and combat-based training such as boxing and kickboxing, while keeping workouts engaging and sustainable around her demanding shooting schedule. Her nutrition, meanwhile, prioritises wholesome home-cooked meals, quality protein, balanced carbohydrates, healthy fats and flexibility, including occasional cheat meals. Nair emphasises building strong foundations over flashy exercises and says fitness should ultimately be functional, sustainable and balanced, allowing people to get stronger and healthier while still enjoying life.

stories.primary_headline: Feeling nostalgic for summer? How to beat the back-to-work blues

primary_source.headline: Feeling nostalgic for summer? How to beat the back-to-work blues
primary_source.content: This time last week, life was very different. You enjoyed late nights, lazy mornings balancing family fun and you time. Even if you enjoy your job, the transition from holiday to work can be hard, particularly in September as the days begin to shorten. Here are some ways of making the transition a little bit easier. It can be tempting to launch straight into tackling the hardest task first. But careers coach Sarah Robinson says it's better to "ease back in" by starting with small, manageable tasks and "quick wins". "It's about trying to build momentum, because I think sometimes it can just feel overwhelming when you've got a massive inbox," she says.

stories.primary_headline: The Bentley Supersports: A stripped-out engineer's indulgence

primary_source.headline: The Bentley Supersports: A stripped-out engineer's indulgence
primary_source.content:
Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Supersports, as well as ride in a preproduction Torcal EV, which we wrote about last week. Ars does not accept paid editorial content.
MONTEREY, Calif.—Last week, we brought news of the Bentley Torcal, a new electric vehicle that the luxury automaker has been cooking up at its HQ in Crewe, England. The company wants to attract new customers with its first battery EV, part of a plan to make sustainability as much a part of the brand's character as its high-end fit and finish. W12 engines have given way to V8 plug-in hybrid power, and the new Continental GT is all the better for it.
But around the same time as Ars got its first experience of that new PHEV two-door on a rather wet Spanish racetrack, some of Bentley's boffins were wondering what might happen if you also built one without the hybrid stuff.
Or all-wheel drive—something that has been a characteristic of every new road-going Bentley since the turn of the century. That would certainly cut the curb weight. So, too, would leaving out the rear seats. That sort of idea leads down a well-trodden path for some OEMs, and Porsche in particular is famous for making stripped-out road cars inspired by its race cars and making money from them, too.Read full article

primary_source.content: Studies have found that anti-inflammatory drugs can improve your mood. If you cut yourself and the area becomes red and swollen, that’s inflammation: immune cells are rushing to fight germs and repair tissue.But inflammation can also occur in the body during illnesses, and a low level of inflammation can arise from obesity or ageing. “A marker of that inflammation tends to be elevated cytokines in people’s blood,” says Prof Daniel M Davis, head of life sciences at Imperial College London and author of Immune Health: A Myth-Busting Guide. “They’re the molecules immune cells use to communicate with each other.” Continue reading...
